version.changelog: v1.2: mem-bridge summarize command, end-to-end examples in README

llm.summary: This memory skill is not malicious, but it should be reviewed because it encourages persistent logging and reuse of user-agent conversations without clear privacy controls.

dimensions.detail: The memory, fuzzy search, summarization, and checkpoint features match the stated purpose, but they are explicitly based on logging prompts and replies and searching stored memory layers, which may include sensitive content.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The artifact documents auto_log, summarize, memory_search, and checkpoint workflows, but does not define consent, retention, deletion, redaction, or limits on what conversations should be logged.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The submitted artifact contains only SKILL.md with no executable scripts, dependencies, package installs, or hidden install behavior; static scan was clean and VirusTotal telemetry was absent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Use of OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE and local memory commands is coherent for a workspace memory tool, but the documented 'search all layers' behavior is broad and not scoped to non-sensitive sessions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The workflow creates cross-session memory through daily layers, summaries from previous logs, and checkpoints, without documented user controls for disabling, pruning, or expiring stored data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent logging prompts and responses into persistent memory. Avoid using it in sessions containing secrets, credentials, personal data, or confidential business information unless you have verified where logs are stored, how to delete them, and how to disable or scope logging.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The finding is supported by the artifact's auto-logging, log summarization, and all-layer search examples. This behavior is expected for a memory skill and is openly described, so it is not malicious, but the missing privacy and retention controls make it a Review concern.
